links.targetTitle: ACs get an opportunity to respond but are explicitly denied

title: Alignment Conservers are derecognized on a 51% likelihood of misalignment, with lenience explicitly barred
content:
A.1.5.4 states that ACs "are held to the highest standard when judging whether their actions are Universally Aligned," and the Action Tenet at A.1.5.4.0.4.1 converts that into a concrete threshold. Facilitators "should acknowledge evidence of misalignment if such evidence is deemed at least 51% more likely than not to be valid," and "should the overall weight of the evidence demonstrate a 51% or greater chance that the AC committed a misaligned act, the Facilitator is **required** to derecognize the AC."

Two features make this severe beyond the numeric threshold. First, derecognition is **mandatory**, not available — the finding compels the sanction, removing the discretion that normally absorbs borderline cases. Second, the Tenet forecloses the standard mitigations: "Any lapse or misjudgment on the part of an AC cannot be excused based on ignorance of the rules, good intentions, honest mistake or similar factors." It goes as far as instructing facilitators to steer "away from notions of 'fairness' or 'lenience.'"

This reads as harsh until placed next to A.0.1.1.12's Slippery Slope Misalignment, which names precisely "the triviality of how the misalignment occurred" and "the good intentions of the actor" as justifications that enable drift. The AC standard is that doctrine applied without exception to the actors who guard the process: the excuses barred here are exactly the excuses the framework identifies as the mechanism of erosion.

The design bet is that the role is replaceable and the equilibrium is not. A bare-majority standard with mandatory removal guarantees false positives — competent conservers will be lost to ambiguous evidence — and the Atlas accepts that as the cheaper error, on the reasoning that ACs are "stewards of Universal Alignment" whose compromise is systemic.

What should temper confidence in it is the Atlas's own admission in NR-1 that protocols for fact-finding and evidence evaluation are missing. A 51% standard is only as meaningful as the evidentiary process producing the 51%.
description: A.1.5.4.0.4.1 makes derecognition mandatory once evidence shows 51% or greater chance of a misaligned act, and rules out ignorance, good intentions, or honest mistake as excuses.
